message: hmm(): every sequence has length 1, so no transition is ever taken and the 2 transition parameter(s) are flat directions of the likelihood - the fit would report a df counting them. A model with one observation per group is a finite mixture: use mixture(gaussian, gaussian), or hold every transition

hmm(init = \stationary\") needs a constant transition matrix, and 'tr12', 'tr22' carries a predictor. A chain whose transition matrix changes from row to row has no single stationary distribution; use init = \"estimated\" or init = \"uniform\""

REML = TRUE cannot be combined with hmm(): REML integrates out the location coefficients, which here are one set per hidden state, and leaves the transition and dispersion parameters outside. The result is a partial restricted likelihood matching no standard definition. Use REML = FALSE

quadrature = TRUE cannot be combined with hmm(): the rule integrates a random effect against a PRODUCT of per-row densities, and an HMM's likelihood is a forward recursion over each sequence, not such a product. Use quadrature = FALSE (Laplace) and check_laplace() to judge the approximation

frmtmb_control(profile = TRUE) cannot be combined with hmm(): profiling moves the state means into an inner Laplace problem, and an HMM likelihood is multimodal in them (the states are exchangeable). Use profile = FALSE
hmm() supports univariate models only: the forward recursion is a likelihood over one response's sequences, and mvbf() / rescor = TRUE would need a joint state process across responses

hmm(): time points must be unique within a sequence; group '1' has 8 rows at time '1'. A Markov chain has one state per time point, so repeated measurements at one time need either a finer time variable or a grouping that separates them
hmm(): ordinal families are not supported as state-dependent distributions ('cumulative'); their thresholds are family-level extra parameters with no per-state copy
hmm(): the state-dependent family cannot be a mixture(); a mixture inside a state is not identified against the state itself
hmm(): the state-dependent family cannot itself be an hmm(); higher-order and hierarchical chains are a different model
hmm() needs the number of hidden states as a whole number of at least 2: hmm(2, gaussian())
hmm(): at most 9 states are supported, because the transition dpar names concatenate the state indices (tr12, tr22, ...) and stop being unambiguous at two digits; K = 12 was given
hmm(): `trans` must be a one-sided formula giving the default predictor of every transition cell, for example trans = ~x
